questiontext.text:
The identity in the exercise above is \(\cos\theta\cot\theta + \sin\theta \equiv \operatorname{cosec}\theta\). For which values of \(\theta\) with \({@lo@}^{\circ} \le \theta \le {@hi@}^{\circ}\) is it not defined?

Enter the set of these values in degrees, for example {30, 45}, or {} if there are none.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
\(\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\) both divide by \(\sin\theta\), so the identity is not defined where \(\sin\theta = 0\): at every multiple of \(180^{\circ}\). In this interval that is \({@ta1@}\). Where \(\cos\theta = 0\) nothing goes wrong: \(\cot\theta = 0\) there.

Wherever \(\sin\theta \ne 0\), the identity itself follows from \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\):

\[\cos\theta\cot\theta + \sin\theta = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta} + \sin\theta = \frac{\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta} = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \operatorname{cosec}\theta.\]

questiondescription.text: This question is directly adapted from Exercise 3 in Section 6 (p. 26) of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022.

node.description: The multiples of 180 in the interval

truefeedback.text: Yes: \(\sin\theta = 0\) at each of these angles, and both \(\cot\theta\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) divide by \(\sin\theta\).

node.description: Diagnostic: the zeros of cos included too

truefeedback.text: You have also included the angles where \(\cos\theta = 0\). There \(\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = 0\), which is defined, and the identity holds: for example, at \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), \(0 \times 0 + 1 = 1 = \operatorname{cosec} 90^{\circ}\).

node.description: Diagnostic: the zeros of cos instead

truefeedback.text: When \(\cos\theta = 0\), \(\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\) is 0, not undefined. The trouble is division by zero: both \(\cot\theta\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) divide by \(\sin\theta\).
Every value you gave is right, but some are missing. Check the whole interval from \({@lo@}^{\circ}\) to \({@hi@}^{\circ}\), including its ends.

falsefeedback.text: The identity is not defined where \(\cot\theta\) or \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) is not defined. Write each of them in terms of \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) and find where a denominator is zero. List every such angle from \({@lo@}^{\circ}\) to \({@hi@}^{\circ}\), and no others.
